# Reconstructed finite leaves at the transitional Rust boundary

Copyright 2026 Masahiko G. Yamada. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

The shared Xor/GHZ/QFT sources require H and CNOT providers whose finite
implementation is independently reconstructed from the artifact. The existing
M2 profile permits a transitional Rust finite-leaf premise, explicitly recorded
until K1/K2 migration; a serialized success flag or handle is not evidence.

Implement the first unitary connection using complete QIRF1/2 bytes, an
independently required legacy type tree, exact input/output owner and ordered
wire interfaces, and an independently supplied exact matrix. Reconstruct all
programs and embedded receipts through the existing finite importer. Derive
output ports from the verifier's final live state, not the input width or a
producer's annotation. Compare exact coefficients, including scalar phase and
zero-width ownership. Share the existing ten-million-unit exact budget across
imports and leaf equations rather than resetting it per packet.

Use a separate new finite API with private result fields; retain the immutable
bytes and complete boundary. This is a Rust finite result only. No Lean theorem
or hierarchy receipt may be fabricated from it. The future host must reconstruct
the same bytes and bind the actual definition/meaning/encoding indices in the
pure M2 checker. Full finite isometries, instruments, multi-owner encodings and
external root binding remain parts of the unchanged 0.2.1 goal.

Validation: independently specified H/CNOT/identity matrices; same-width wrong
type trees, output order and owner mutations; global phase on Unit; malformed
or forged QIRF evidence; source metadata binding; exact arithmetic/capacity and
shared-budget exhaustion; reconstruction from independent buffers. Keep existing
finite-interface behavior and public Rust enum variants unchanged.
